text: A teacher reads your surname off the register and sighs. 'I taught the last one of you. And the one before.'

right.label: Live it down
right.result: By Friday the sigh has a new reason.

up.label: Change your name by deed poll

risk.result: Your family doesn't take it well.

text: 'Your family has always done well,' says the careers teacher, looking at your marks over her glasses. 'Until now.'

right.label: Break the chain
right.result: Somebody had to. You feel almost historic.

up.label: Found your own company on day one

risk.result: The company folds. The family notices.

text: The portrait of the one who left you everything hangs in the hall. The eyes follow you. So does the disappointment.

left.label: Take it down
left.result: It leaves a pale square on the wall. The square also judges you.

right.label: Leave it up
right.result: You nod at it every morning. It has not nodded back.

risk.result: The family does not approve of the likeness.

text: In a drawer: the family watch. It stopped the minute its last owner did. A dealer turns it over and offers $4,000.

left.label: Sell it
left.result: The dealer sells it on for nine. You learn this at a bad moment.

right.label: Wear it
right.result: It is never right. You are late for everything, with dignity.

up.label: Take it to be repaired and keep it ticking

risk.result: It was priceless. It's now worthless.

text: A cousin you've never met says the will was wrong and wants their share. They've brought a folder. It's colour-coded.

risk.result: It was a very good folder.

right.label: Pay them off
right.result: They send a Christmas card every year now. It always mentions the folder.

up.label: Offer them half and a seat on the board

risk.result: They take half and then sue for the rest.

text: The family plot at the cemetery has one space left. The office rings, very cheerful, to ask if you'd like to reserve it.

left.label: Reserve it
left.result: Your name is on a list. It is the one waiting list you are in no hurry on.

right.label: Hang up
right.result: They ring again next year. They are patient people.

up.label: Buy a second plot beside it

risk.result: You can't stop thinking about the extra one.

text: Every year your family eats the same grey pudding on the same day. Nobody likes it. This year it's your turn to make it.

left.label: Make it
left.result: It is as bad as ever. Everyone is delighted.

right.label: Order pizza
right.result: Your aunt does not speak to you until spring.

risk.result: A family rift that outlasts pudding.

text: On an old door frame, a parent's height marks in pencil, year by year. At your age they were taller. By a lot.

right.label: Add your mark
right.result: You stand very straight. It doesn't help.

up.label: Frame the whole door and put it in the hall

risk.result: The door was holding up the wall.

text: An old neighbour tells you your family is cursed: not one of you has ever died peacefully. She says it kindly, with tea.

risk.result: You trip on their step on the way out. Coincidence.

right.label: See a priest
right.result: The priest says it's nonsense, then blesses you twice to be safe.

up.label: Break the curse in a midnight ritual

risk.result: The ritual cost a fortune. The curse stays.

text: In the attic: a letter marked 'to be opened when I am gone'. You open it, heart racing. It is mostly about the boiler.

left.label: Read on

risk.result: There was a catch.

left.result: The last line is about you. It is better than the boiler part.

right.label: Put it back
right.result: You still don't know how the boiler works.

up.label: Read it aloud at the next family dinner

risk.result: The secret is out. Everyone speaks at once.

text: A relative has heard you came into money. They have a business idea and a slideshow. It involves alpacas. Many alpacas.

left.label: Invest
left.result: You own a share of eleven alpacas.

risk.result: Alpacas, it turns out, are in.

right.label: Decline
right.result: They tell the whole family you've changed.

risk.result: The herd eats the garden. The wool is wrong.

text: A website offers to trace your family tree for $200. The ad says one in five people find a pirate. Or worse.

risk.result: Seven generations of people who died of things you also have.

up.label: Hire a genealogist to dig deeper

risk.result: You find a second family. Awkward.

text: Family reunion. Forty relatives, one barbecue, paper plates, and an uncle with opinions and a folding chair.

left.label: Go
left.result: You are told you look tired by nine separate people.

up.label: Take the stage and give a speech

risk.result: The uncle heckles. Then the cousin. Then the dog.

text: A man at a market stall sells you your family crest. It has a lion on it. Nobody in your family has ever met a lion.

left.label: Buy it
left.result: It goes above the toilet. The lion looks unsure.

up.label: Commission your own and sue them

risk.result: The crest was real. The lawyer is not.

text: A local historian wants to write a book about your family. Pen ready, they ask if there's anything you'd like left out.

left.label: Tell all
left.result: Chapter six ends two friendships and one marriage. Not yours.

right.label: Leave things out
right.result: The book is short and very polite.

risk.result: Your aunt reads chapter three. She stops speaking to you.

text: The council offers a bench with your family name on it for $900. You're not dead, but they suggest planning ahead.

left.label: Buy it
left.result: You sit on it most days. Checking the quality.

risk.result: The council won't allow it. Only the bench.
